def rep(p,R):
    s=open(p).read()
    for a,b in R:
        assert s.count(a)==1,(p,a[:60]); s=s.replace(a,b)
    open(p,'w').write(s)
rep('chapter_01/CH-01-knowledge-authority-execution.md',[
("A **confirmation request** (the mechanism asks, a person decides) is not a block, **provided the person asked holds a grant covering the decision**.",
 "A **confirmation request** (the mechanism asks, a person decides) is not a block, **provided the person asked holds a grant covering the decision and the confirmation is recorded as an act** (who confirmed, when, under which grant). A confirmation that leaves no record, such as a dismissed dialog box, is a **report**, not an act (INV-A1). It cannot lift a block [PC L159–161]."),
("- **If** read access is governed, context assembly must filter by may-read before relevance (conditional revision of Ch. 0 §0.7, step 2). Otherwise the assembled context leaks what the reader may not know, whatever its relevance.",
 "- **If** read access is governed, context assembly must filter by may-read before relevance (conditional revision of Ch. 0 §0.7, step 2). Otherwise the assembled context leaks what the reader may not know, whatever its relevance. A later source proposes the same mechanism as a \"context assembly policy\", with the rule that **the policy filters and never elevates**: an assembled context may contain less than the actor could reach, never more [PC L118–128]. This is §1.7's \"derivation may narrow, never widen\" applied to assembly. Its second rule, that provenance travels into the package, is already required by Ch. 0 §0.7 (step 3). Whether read access is governed at all remains open (OQ-25)."),
])
rep('chapter_02/CH-02-rules-and-conflict.md',[
("| E6 | **not analysable** in the logic used (undecided, time-out), or **not readable** (see V3 addition below) | UNKNOWN | RM, Ch. 2 §2.3(a); V3 L292 |",
 "| E6 | **not analysable**: (a) **undecidable or unresolved** in the logic used; (b) **resource-exhausted** (time-out): the analysis gave up, so the domain may be perfectly decidable; or (c) **not readable** (see V3 addition below). Kept apart because the remedies differ: (a) needs a better model or more information, (b) needs more resources [PC L77–87] | UNKNOWN · TIMEOUT | RM, Ch. 2 §2.3(a); V3 L292; PC L77–87 |"),
("A gap between hardness and enforcement consequence is normal during migration (\"advisory today; blocking once the gate is trusted\", RS L181–183).",
 """A gap between hardness and enforcement consequence is normal during migration ("advisory today; blocking once the gate is trusted", RS L181–183).

**Override, a further independent property (Src, PROPOSED; PC L147–163).** Whether a block may be **lifted case by case** is not a degree of hardness. A HARD gate may allow an override and still default to refusal. A later source therefore adds **override: none | recorded act**, and insists that a user's on-screen confirmation is not enough: "a UI confirmation is a report", so the override must be a **recorded act** [PC L161]. *Analysis (Ded):* this follows from "a report of an act is not the act" (INV-A1, Ch. 1 §1.12) and from recognition requiring a record (I-2). Which gates allow override, and which acts qualify, is open (PC's OQ-29).

**Results that may open a gate (Src, PROPOSED; PC L77–87).** Of the analysis results proven conflict · proven consistent · unknown · not applicable · time-out, **only "proven consistent" satisfies a HARD gate**. This is the guard principle of §2.8.7 (positive evidence of the permitting condition) applied to analysis results. **Time-out is the case most tempting to treat as a pass**, which is why it is named separately."""),
])
print('ok')
